transcription.tex: 5 Point \(X\) has coordinates \((7,-2)\) and point \(Y\) has coordinates \((4,q)\). The perpendicular bisector of \(XY\) has equation \(y=4x+b\). Find the value of \(q\) and the value of \(b\).

transcription.tex: \(X(7,-2)\) and \(Y(4,q)\)\[\text{The gradient of the line segment }XY=\frac{y_2-y_1}{x_2-x_1}=\frac{q-(-2)}{4-7}=\frac{q+2}{-3}\]From the equation of the perpendicular bisector of PQ, \(y=4x+b\), the gradient is 4. Therefore, the gradient of \(XY=-\frac14\), so \(-\frac14=\frac{q+2}{-3}\).\[q=-\frac54\]\[\text{Midpoint of }XY=\left(\frac{7+4}2,\frac{-2+(-\frac54)}2\right)=\left(\frac{11}2,-\frac{13}8\right)\]Substituting \(x=\frac{11}2\) and \(y=-\frac{13}8\) into \(y=4x+b\) gives\[-\frac{13}8=4\left(\frac{11}2\right)+b,\qquad b=-\frac{189}8\]So \(b=-\frac{189}8,\ q=-\frac54\).

transcription.tex: \textbf{a} The centre of the circle \((x+4)^2+(y-1)^2=242\) is \((-4,1)\). The gradient of the line joining \((-4,1)\) and \((7,-10)\) is\[\frac{y_2-y_1}{x_2-x_1}=\frac{-10-1}{7-(-4)}=\frac{-11}{7+4}=-\frac{11}{11}=-1\]The gradient of the tangent is \(\frac{-1}{(-1)}=1\).

transcription.tex: The equation of the tangent is\[\begin{aligned}y-y_1&=m(x-x_1)\\y-(-10)&=1(x-7)\\y+10&=x-7\\y&=x-17\end{aligned}\]

transcription.tex: 9 A circle has equation \(x^2+2x+y^2-24y-24=0\).\par a Find the centre and radius of the circle.\par b The points \(A(-13,17)\) and \(B(11,7)\) both lie on the circumference of the circle. Show that \(AB\) is a diameter of the circle.\par c The point \(C\) lies on the negative \(x\)-axis and the angle \(ACB=90^\circ\). Find the coordinates of \(C\).
transcription.notes: Visually transcribed original text and mathematics.

transcription.tex: \textbf{a} \(x^2+2x+y^2-24y-24=0\). Completing the square gives:\[\begin{aligned}(x+1)^2-1+(y-12)^2-144-24&=0\\(x+1)^2+(y-12)^2&=169\end{aligned}\]Centre of the circle is \((-1,12)\) and the radius of the circle is 13.\par\textbf{b} If \(AB\) is the diameter of the circle then the midpoint of AB is the centre of the circle.\[\text{Midpoint of }AB=\left(\frac{-13+11}2,\frac{17+7}2\right)=(-1,12)\]Therefore, \(AB\) is the diameter of the circle.\par\textbf{c} The point \(C\) lies on the \(x\)-axis, so \(y=0\). Substitute \(y=0\) into the equation of the circle.\[\begin{aligned}(x+1)^2+(0-12)^2&=169\\x^2+2x+1+144&=169\\x^2+2x-24&=0\\(x+6)(x-4)&=0\\x=-6,\quad x&=4\end{aligned}\]As \(x\) is negative, \(x=-6\). The coordinates of \(C\) are \((-6,0)\).
